scenes.text: A ditch through the desert cut the trip from Britain to India roughly in half.
The Suez Canal opened on November seventeenth, eighteen sixty nine.
It links the Mediterranean to the Red Sea, so ships skip the long trip around Africa.
The project was led by a French diplomat named Ferdinand de Lesseps.
Digging began in April eighteen fifty nine and took about ten years.
For years, Egyptian peasants were forced to dig, and many died of diseases like cholera.
Napoleon's surveyors had wrongly thought the Red Sea was about eight meters higher.
In fact both seas sit at about the same level, so the canal has no locks.
At the opening, French Empress Eugenie led the parade of ships on her yacht.
It was about one hundred sixty four kilometers long back then.
Today it's about one hundred ninety three.
In twenty twenty one, the giant ship Ever Given got stuck sideways.
For about six days, more than a hundred ships waited at each end.
Today, roughly a tenth of the world's trade passes through this one strip of water.
Which other shortcut changed the world the most?

title: The Suez Canal cut the trip to India in half 🚢
caption: The Suez Canal opened on Nov 17, 1869 after about 10 years of digging. It has no locks, and roughly a tenth of world trade uses it.
